title: COVID-19 Lockdowns Trigger France's Deepest Recession Since World War II
reason: All material facts confirmed via independent sources. INSEE's own release confirms Q1 2020 GDP fell 5.8% (initial estimate; later revised to -5.9%), the sharpest quarterly fall since records began in 1949, driven by the shutdown of non-essential activity under the nationwide lockdown that began March 17, 2020. This followed a Q4 2019 contraction of -0.1%, meeting the technical definition of recession (two consecutive quarters of decline). Q2 2020 deepened further with GDP falling 13.8% (a new record), as lockdown continued through early May. INSEE's later "French economy in 2020: a year of upheaval" analysis states full-year 2020 GDP fell 7.9% (the widely cited final/revised figure; an even earlier flash estimate was -8.3%), explicitly characterized across sources as France's sharpest annual decline since the end of WWII. Tourism, transport, and hospitality (accommodation/food service) are consistently identified across INSEE and news sources as among the hardest-hit sectors due to travel restrictions and closures. All magnitudes, dates, and sequencing in the description match documented record.
